title: New archaeobotanical data from the Early Neolithic sites of Dja’de el-Mughara and Tell Aswad (Syria)
lineage: Author-hosted copy of the version of record. The study uses a subset of secure contexts and revises an earlier published analysis that also involved Willcox.

passages.note: Using secure Pre-Pottery Neolithic B contexts and a revised stratigraphy, the authors report that domestic-type barley spikelet bases first form a substantial share in phase AW2. Table 1 dates AW2 to approximately 8200–7500 cal BCE.
